trade: watches, jewelry, engravings and fancy goods

proprietors.name: Louis Chevalier
proprietors.basis: ADOPTED, NOT MINTED. Louis Chevalier is the reconstructed trade head the resident band's `trade_households` stage drew at watchmaker in the west division (slot trade_households:persons/male/50_plus/west/family/trade:watchmaker:002), and that card says itself that the business band adopts these heads rather than minting its own. One quota, filled once: this house is the establishment that head keeps.

locations.basis: A FACE, NOT A PREMISES. The placement rule for a silversmith_jeweller kept by a west-division household deals this house onto Canal Street; the face is drawn on the seed printed in `reconstruction.seed` from the faces that rule allows, and no lot, roof or coordinate is claimed. T-1195 writes the placement policy with its evidence and T-1199 seats this house on the lot grid.
locations.limit_reason: No source places this house, because no source names it: it exists because the December 1835 State census counts more of its class than the register holds. The street is the reconstruction's own deal and stops there.

dates.basis: NOTHING DATES THIS HOUSE. The census that orders it was taken in December 1835 and counts a standing trade, not an opening; the record claims that the house was trading on 1835-07-01 and nothing about either end.

proprietor_community.basis: The 1 keeper(s) this record names and the resident layer holds a card for all read french_canadian: Louis Chevalier (french_canadian). A house is not its keeper, so the reading is an inference about the house and is capped there.

replaceable_by: A register, directory or deed naming a real house of this class in the west division in 1835 — that house takes this slot and this record is withdrawn.

basis.note: the December 1835 State census prints 2; the register holds 1 at the scene date. The book leaves 1 of this class to reconstruct and this is one of them. The style is dealt on the seed printed beside it from the period forms the register itself carries: the initial-and-surname signature is the commonest in the corpus, and the one attested house of this class signs by surname — 'J. H. Mulford'. The goods line is J. H. Mulford's own trade line in the register — the one attested house of the class, and the only goods line the corpus prints for it.

reconstruction.withdrawn_if: a source naming a real house of this class, or a re-cut of the order book that no longer orders this bucket; the retirement runs through --build, never by hand
